greek: Ἀνέβη δὲ Αβραμ ἐξ Αἰγύπτου, αὐτὸς καὶ ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ καὶ πάντα τὰ αὐτοῦ καὶ Λωτ μετʼ αὐτοῦ, εἰς τὴν ἔρημον.
hint: Abram goes up out of Egypt into the desert, with Lot.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *hannegbâ*, *into the Negeb*, the south. The Greek has *into the desert*, as at 12:9.
*All the of him*: the article with the genitive and no noun, *all that was his*.
Glossed again, first in this chapter.

reading: [[went up|went up, mounted, went up to, embarked]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[name:Αβραμ]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from]] [[name:Αἰγύπτου]], he and [[the woman|the woman, the mistress and lady, the wife and spouse]] of him and [[all|all, the whole, every, every single]] the of him and [[name:Λωτ]] [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of]] him, [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[the desert part|the desert part, the desolate, the lone and lonely and lonesome and solitary, the helpless, the reft and void and destitute, the undefended]].

names.gloss: (Αβραμ, from Hebrew ʾAbrām, "the father is exalted")
(Αἴγυπτος, the Greek name of the land; Hebrew Miṣrayim)
(Λωτ, from Hebrew Lôṭ, of uncertain meaning)

greek: Αβραμ δὲ ἦν πλούσιος σφόδρα κτήνεσιν καὶ ἀργυρίῳ καὶ χρυσίῳ.
hint: Abram is very rich in cattle, silver and gold.

notes.text: The Hebrew *kābēd mĕʾōd*, *very heavy*. The Greek has πλούσιος, *rich*.

reading: [[name:Αβραμ]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], was, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, [[rich|rich, wealthy, opulent, rich in, richly furnished, ample and abundant]] [[very|very, very much, exceedingly, violently, far, most certainly]] [[with flocks and herds|with flocks and herds, with single beasts, with oxen, with sheep, with beasts for riding]] and [[with a piece of silver|with a piece of silver, with a silver coin, with money and a sum of money and cash, with silver]] and [[with a piece of gold|with a piece of gold, with gold, with gold coin and money]].

greek: καὶ ἐπορεύθη ὅθεν ἦλθεν, εἰς τὴν ἔρημον ἕως Βαιθηλ, ἕως τοῦ τόπου, οὗ ἦν ἡ σκηνὴ αὐτοῦ τὸ πρότερον, ἀνὰ μέσον Βαιθηλ καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον Αγγαι,
hint: He goes back to the place of his tent between Bethel and Ai.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *lĕmassāʿāyw minnegeb*, *by his stages from the Negeb*. The Greek has *from where he came, into the desert*.
The neuter of πρότερος used as an adverb, *before*; the article as printed.

greek: εἰς τὸν τόπον τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου, οὗ ἐποίησεν ἐκεῖ τὴν ἀρχήν· καὶ ἐπεκαλέσατο ἐκεῖ Αβραμ τὸ ὄνομα κυρίου.
hint: At the altar Abram calls on the name of the Lord.

notes.text: The Hebrew *ʾăšer-ʿāśâ šām bāriʾšōnâ*, *which he had made there at the first*. The Greek makes *the beginning* the object: *where he made there the beginning*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads τὴν σκηνήν, *the tent*; ἀρχήν is the Berlin papyrus's, 911.

reading: [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[the place|the place, the local circumstances, the position, the passage in a book, the topic, the common-place, the occasion and opportunity]] of the altar, where [[made|fashioned, wrought, produced, performed, did]] [[there|there, in that place]] [[the beginning|the beginning, the origin, the first cause, the headship and rule and governing precedence]]; and [[called upon|called upon, invoked and appealed to, invited, called in as a helper, was called by surname]] [[there|there, in that place]] [[name:Αβραμ]] [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression]] [[of lord|of lord, of master, of the one having power and authority over]].

greek: καὶ Λωτ τῷ συμπορευομένῳ μετὰ Αβραμ ἦν πρόβατα καὶ βόες καὶ σκηναί.
hint: Lot too has flocks, cattle and tents.

notes.text: [[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads κτήνη, *cattle*; σκηναί is the Berlin papyrus's, 911.

reading: and to [[name:Λωτ]] [[to the one going|to the one going, to the one journeying together, to the one coming together]] [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of]] [[name:Αβραμ]] was [[things that walk forward|things that walk forward, cattle, flocks and herds, horses, small cattle, sheep]] and [[cows|cows, oxen, kine and cattle, ox-hide shields]] and [[covered places|covered places, tents, camps, dwelling-places, temples]].

greek: καὶ οὐκ ἐχώρει αὐτοὺς ἡ γῆ κατοικεῖν ἅμα, ὅτι ἦν τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτῶν πολλά, καὶ οὐκ ἐδύναντο κατοικεῖν ἅμα.
hint: The land cannot hold them both.

notes.text: χωρέω is first *to make room for another, give way*; *to hold, contain*, the verse's sense, is the entry's last.

reading: and not [[was making room for another|was making room for another, was giving way and drawing back and retiring and withdrawing, was putting back and retiring, was giving way to, was retiring before, was going forward and moving on, was going and coming, was going on one's journey and travelling, was coming to, was coming on and beginning, was passing and near an end, was going on and advancing, was coming to an issue and turning out, was going on well and succeeding, was spreading abroad, was spreading, was having room for, was holding and containing]] them [[the earth|the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]] [[to dwell in|to dwell in, to settle in, to colonise, to inhabit, to settle and dwell, to lie and be situate]] [[at once|at once, at the same time, at the same time with and together with]], [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as]] was, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, [[the existing circumstances|the existing circumstances, the present advantages, what belongs to one, the possessions and means]] of them [[many|many, often, much and mighty and great, deep, loud, strong, large and wide, far, long]], and not [[were being able|were being able, were capable and strong enough, were powerful and mighty, were having influence, were daring and bearing, were passing for, were worth, were equivalent to, were signifying and meaning, were availing]] [[to dwell in|to dwell in, to settle in, to colonise, to inhabit, to settle and dwell, to lie and be situate]] [[at once|at once, at the same time, at the same time with and together with]].

greek: καὶ ἐγένετο μάχη ἀνὰ μέσον τῶν ποιμένων τῶν κτηνῶν τοῦ Αβραμ καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον τῶν ποιμένων τῶν κτηνῶν τοῦ Λωτ· οἱ δὲ Χαναναῖοι καὶ οἱ Φερεζαῖοι τότε κατῴκουν τὴν γῆν.
hint: Strife between the herdsmen; the Canaanites and Perizzites in the land.

notes.text: The Hebrew *rîb*, *a dispute*. μάχη is first *battle, fight*.

reading: and [[came into being|came to be, arose, was brought into existence]] [[battle|battle, fight and combat, quarrels and strifes and wranglings, a contest, a struggle, a mode of fighting and way of battle, a field of battle]] [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two]] [[of the herdsmen|of the herdsmen, of the shepherds, of the captains and chiefs, of the masters and lords, of the pastors and teachers]] [[of the flocks and herds|of the flocks and herds, of the single beasts, of the oxen, of the sheep, of the beasts for riding]] of [[name:Αβραμ]] and [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two]] [[of the herdsmen|of the herdsmen, of the shepherds, of the captains and chiefs, of the masters and lords, of the pastors and teachers]] [[of the flocks and herds|of the flocks and herds, of the single beasts, of the oxen, of the sheep, of the beasts for riding]] of [[name:Λωτ]]; [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[name:Χαναναῖοι]] and [[name:Φερεζαῖοι]] [[at that time|at that time, then, in those times and formerly, at one time]] [[were dwelling in|were dwelling in, were settling in, were colonising, were inhabiting, were settling and dwelling, were lying and situate]] [[the earth|the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]].

names.gloss: (Φερεζαῖος, from Hebrew Pĕrizzî, usually connected with pĕrāzî, "a villager")

greek: εἶπεν δὲ Αβραμ τῷ Λωτ Μὴ ἔστω μάχη ἀνὰ μέσον ἐμοῦ καὶ σοῦ καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον τῶν ποιμένων μου καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον τῶν ποιμένων σου, ὅτι ἄνθρωποι ἀδελφοὶ ἡμεῖς ἐσμεν.
hint: Let there be no strife: we are brothers.

notes.text: The Hebrew *ʾănāšîm ʾaḥîm*, *men, brothers*, two nouns side by side, as the Greek keeps them.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus exchanges μου and the second σου: *the herdsmen of you and … the herdsmen of me*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[name:Αβραμ]] to [[name:Λωτ]] not let be [[battle|battle, fight and combat, quarrels and strifes and wranglings, a contest, a struggle, a mode of fighting and way of battle, a field of battle]] [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two]] of me and of you and [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two]] [[of the herdsmen|of the herdsmen, of the shepherds, of the captains and chiefs, of the masters and lords, of the pastors and teachers]] of me and [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two]] [[of the herdsmen|of the herdsmen, of the shepherds, of the captains and chiefs, of the masters and lords, of the pastors and teachers]] of you, [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as]] [[men|men, human beings]] [[sons of the same mother|sons of the same mother, brothers, near kinsmen]] we are.

greek: οὐκ ἰδοὺ πᾶσα ἡ γῆ ἐναντίον σού ἐστιν; διαχωρίσθητι ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ· εἰ σὺ εἰς ἀριστερά, ἐγὼ εἰς δεξιά· εἰ δὲ σὺ εἰς δεξιά, ἐγὼ εἰς ἀριστερά.
hint: The whole land is before you: go left or right.

notes.text: διαχωρίζω, *to separate*, one sense, plain text, in the passive imperative.

Neuter plurals used as nouns, so each takes its entry's first noun sense, anarthrous: ἀριστερός *left*, which is also its first sense; δεξιός *right*, from *the right*, where its first sense is *on the right hand*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads καί for οὐκ, and alone leaves out ἐστιν.

reading: not [[lo|lo, behold, see there]] [[all|all, the whole, every, every single]] [[the earth|the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]] [[in the presence of|in the presence of, before, opposite and face to face, against]] of you is? be separated [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] me; if you [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[left|left and on the left, the left hand, boding ill and ominous]], I [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[right|right, on the right hand, fortunate and boding good and lucky, dexterous and ready, sharp and shrewd and clever]]; if [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], you [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[right|right, on the right hand, fortunate and boding good and lucky, dexterous and ready, sharp and shrewd and clever]], I [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[left|left and on the left, the left hand, boding ill and ominous]].

greek: καὶ ἐπάρας Λωτ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ εἶδεν πᾶσαν τὴν περίχωρον τοῦ Ιορδάνου ὅτι πᾶσα ἦν ποτιζομένη — πρὸ τοῦ καταστρέψαι τὸν θεὸν Σοδομα καὶ Γομορρα — ὡς ὁ παράδεισος τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ὡς ἡ γῆ Αἰγύπτου ἕως ἐλθεῖν εἰς Ζογορα.
hint: Lot sees the watered plain of the Jordan, like the garden of God.

notes.lemma: τὸν θεὸν … ὡς ὁ παράδεισος τοῦ θεοῦ
notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew has *YHWH* both times: *before YHWH destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, like the garden of YHWH*. The Greek has ὁ θεός both times, and for *gan* the παράδεισος of 2:8.

notes.lemma: — πρὸ τοῦ καταστρέψαι τὸν θεὸν Σοδομα καὶ Γομορρα —
notes.text: Rahlfs sets the clause between dashes, as the Hebrew sets it apart; the reading keeps it in commas, since dashes mark the chains.
περίχωρος is an adjective, *round about a place*; used as a noun it is *the people about* in the masculine, *the country round about* in the feminine, which the verse has.

reading: and [[having lifted up and set on|having lifted up and set on, having lifted and raised, having exalted and magnified, having stirred up and excited, having induced and persuaded]] [[name:Λωτ]] [[the eyes|the eyes, the sight, the dearest and best, the buds]] of him [[saw|saw, perceived, beheld, looked at]] [[all|all, the whole, every, every single]] [[the country round about|the country round about, the round about a place, the people about]] of [[name:Ιορδάνου]] [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as]] [[all|all, the whole, every, every single]] was, and kept on being, [[being given to drink|being given to drink, being watered]], [[before|before, in front of, further on, sooner, rather than]] [[to turn down|to turn down and trample on, to turn the soil, to upset and overturn, to subject to oneself and subdue, to turn back and bring back, to turn round and bring to an end, to come to an end and die, to twist up, to be subdued]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] [[name:Σοδομα]] and [[name:Γομορρα]], [[as|as, according as, considering, like]] [[the park|the park, the garden of Eden, paradise]] [[of the God|of him who is God definitively, of the one the article marks out, of the known and the only]] and [[as|as, according as, considering, like]] [[the earth|the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]] of [[name:Αἰγύπτου]] [[until|until, till, while, so long as]] [[to come|to come, to go, to go back and return, to be going to and intend, to come within a little of and be near]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[name:Ζογορα]].

names.gloss: (Ἰορδάνης, from Hebrew Yardēn, usually connected with yārad, "to go down")
(Σόδομα, from Hebrew Sĕdōm, of uncertain meaning)
(Γόμορρα, from Hebrew ʿĂmōrâ, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ ἐξελέξατο ἑαυτῷ Λωτ πᾶσαν τὴν περίχωρον τοῦ Ιορδάνου, καὶ ἀπῆρεν Λωτ ἀπὸ ἀνατολῶν, καὶ διεχωρίσθησαν ἕκαστος ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ.
hint: Lot chooses the plain of the Jordan and moves east.

notes.text: The middle's own sense is *to pick out for oneself*; ἑαυτῷ, *for himself*, says it again, and the reading keeps both.
διαχωρίζω, *to separate*, one sense, plain text.

reading: and [[picked out for himself|picked out for himself, chose out, pulled out]] for himself [[name:Λωτ]] [[all|all, the whole, every, every single]] [[the country round about|the country round about, the round about a place, the people about]] of [[name:Ιορδάνου]], and [[lifted off|lifted off, carried off, took away, removed from, led away, sailed and marched away and departed, departed from, set out on]] [[name:Λωτ]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[of risings|of risings, of rises, of the quarter of sunrise, of the east]], and were separated [[every|every, every one, each, each one, all and each one, singly and by itself, each by himself]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[of the son of the same mother|of the son of the same mother, of the brother, of the near kinsman]] of him.

greek: Αβραμ δὲ κατῴκησεν ἐν γῇ Χανααν, Λωτ δὲ κατῴκησεν ἐν πόλει τῶν περιχώρων καὶ ἐσκήνωσεν ἐν Σοδομοις·
hint: Abram stays in Canaan; Lot pitches his tent in Sodom.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wayyeʾĕhal ʿad-sĕdōm*, *and pitched his tent as far as Sodom*. The Greek has *in Sodom*.
σκηνόω, *to pitch tents*: the form of John 1:14, καὶ ἐσκήνωσεν ἐν ἡμῖν.

reading: [[name:Αβραμ]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[dwelt in|dwelt in, settled in, colonised, inhabited, settled and dwelt, lay and was situate]] [[in earth|within, inside of, and by means of earth, land, the ground]] [[name:Χανααν]], [[name:Λωτ]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[dwelt in|dwelt in, settled in, colonised, inhabited, settled and dwelt, lay and was situate]] [[in city|within, inside of, and by means of city, citadel, country, body of citizens, state]] [[of the countries round about|of the countries round about, of the round about a place, of the people about]] and [[pitched tents|pitched tents and encamped, dwelt in a tent, settled and took up one's abode, lived, occupied with tents]] in [[name:Σοδομοις]];

names.gloss: (Χανααν, from Hebrew Kĕnaʿan, of uncertain meaning)

greek: οἱ δὲ ἄνθρωποι οἱ ἐν Σοδομοις πονηροὶ καὶ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἐναντίον τοῦ θεοῦ σφόδρα.
hint: The men of Sodom are wicked and sinful before God.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *laYHWH*, *against YHWH*; the Greek has *before the God*.
πονηρός is first *toilsome*, as at 2:9; ἁμαρτωλός, *sinful*, and as a noun *a sinner*.

reading: [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[the men|the men, the human beings, mankind]] the in [[name:Σοδομοις]] [[toilsome|toilsome, painful, grievous, good-for-nothing, bad and worthless, wicked]] and [[sinful|sinful, sinners]] [[in the presence of|in the presence of, before, opposite and face to face, against]] [[of the God|of him who is God definitively, of the one the article marks out, of the known and the only]] [[very|very, very much, exceedingly, violently, far, most certainly]].

greek: Ὁ δὲ θεὸς εἶπεν τῷ Αβραμ μετὰ τὸ διαχωρισθῆναι τὸν Λωτ ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ Ἀναβλέψας τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς σου ἰδὲ ἀπὸ τοῦ τόπου, οὗ νῦν σὺ εἶ, πρὸς βορρᾶν καὶ λίβα καὶ ἀνατολὰς καὶ θάλασσαν·
hint: God tells Abram to look north, south-west, east and west.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *waYHWH*; the Greek has ὁ θεός.

notes.lemma: πρὸς βορρᾶν καὶ λίβα καὶ ἀνατολὰς καὶ θάλασσαν
notes.text: The Hebrew *ṣāpōnâ wānegbâ wāqēdmâ wāyāmmâ*, *north, south, east and west*. The Greek names the quarters by the north wind, βορρᾶς, filed under Βορέας; the south-west wind, λίψ, one sense and plain text; the sunrise; and the sea.
The aorist imperative of ὁράω, *see*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads Ἀνάβλεψον … καὶ ἰδέ; the participle is Coislinianus's, M.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only]] [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] to [[name:Αβραμ]] [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after]] to be separated [[name:Λωτ]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] him [[having looked up|having looked up, having looked, having looked up at, having cast up, having recovered one's sight]] [[with the eyes|with the eyes, with the sight, with the dearest and best, with the buds]] of you [[see|see, perceive, behold, look at]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[of the place|of the place, of the local circumstances, of the position, of the passage in a book, of the topic, of the common-place, of the occasion and opportunity]], where [[now|now, even now, just now]] you are, [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward]] [[north wind|north wind, the north, northward]] and south-west wind and [[risings|risings, rises, the quarter of sunrise, the east]] and [[sea|sea, the Mediterranean, a well of salt water]];

greek: ὅτι πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν, ἣν σὺ ὁρᾷς, σοὶ δώσω αὐτὴν καὶ τῷ σπέρματί σου ἕως τοῦ αἰῶνος.
hint: All the land you see I will give to you and your seed for ever.

notes.text: As at 12:7, the words Paul reads as singular at Galatians 3:16: Καὶ τῷ σπέρματί σου, ὅς ἐστιν Χριστός.

reading: [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as]] [[all|all, the whole, every, every single]] [[the earth|the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]], which you [[you see|you see, you perceive, you behold, you look at]], to you [[I will give|I will give, I will grant, I will provide, I will give over and deliver up]] it and [[to that which is sown|to that which is sown, to the seed, to the germ and origin and element, to the offspring and issue, to the race and descent]] of you [[until|until, till, while, so long as]] [[of the period of existence|of the period of existence, of the life-time and life, of the age and generation, of the long space of time, of the era and epoch, of the world]].

greek: καὶ ποιήσω τὸ σπέρμα σου ὡς τὴν ἄμμον τῆς γῆς· εἰ δύναταί τις ἐξαριθμῆσαι τὴν ἄμμον τῆς γῆς, καὶ τὸ σπέρμα σου ἐξαριθμηθήσεται.
hint: Abram's seed will be as the sand of the earth.

notes.text: ἐξαριθμέω, *to count throughout, number*: the verb, and then its passive.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads ἀριθμηθήσεται, without ἐξ; the Berlin papyrus, 911, has it.

reading: and [[I will make|I will make, I will do, I will produce, I will create]] [[that which is sown|that which is sown, the seed, the germ and origin and element, the offspring and issue, the race and descent]] of you [[as|as, according as, considering, like]] [[the sand|the sand, the sandy ground and race-course]] [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]]; if [[is able|is able, is capable and strong enough, is powerful and mighty, has influence, dares and bears, passes for, is worth, is equivalent to, signifies and means, avails]] [[any one|any one, some one, many a one, each one, every man]] [[to count throughout|to count throughout, to number, to count out and pay in ready money]] [[the sand|the sand, the sandy ground and race-course]] [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]], also [[that which is sown|that which is sown, the seed, the germ and origin and element, the offspring and issue, the race and descent]] of you [[will be counted throughout|will be counted throughout, will be numbered, will be counted out and paid in ready money]].

greek: ἀναστὰς διόδευσον τὴν γῆν εἴς τε τὸ μῆκος αὐτῆς καὶ εἰς τὸ πλάτος, ὅτι σοὶ δώσω αὐτήν.
hint: Rise and walk through the land.

notes.text: διοδεύω, *to travel through*, one sense, plain text, as at 12:6.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus adds at the end καὶ τῷ σπέρματί σου εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.

reading: [[having stood up|having stood up, having risen, having risen to fight against, having risen to go and set out]] travel through [[the earth|the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] both [[the length|the length, the distances, the height and tallness and stature]] of it and [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[the breadth|the breadth, the width]], [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as]] to you [[I will give|I will give, I will grant, I will provide, I will give over and deliver up]] it.

greek: καὶ ἀποσκηνώσας Αβραμ ἐλθὼν κατῴκησεν παρὰ τὴν δρῦν τὴν Μαμβρη, ἣ ἦν ἐν Χεβρων, καὶ ᾠκοδόμησεν ἐκεῖ θυσιαστήριον κυρίῳ.
hint: Abram settles by the oak of Mamre at Hebron and builds an altar.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *bĕʾēlōnê mamrēʾ*, *by the oaks of Mamre*, plural. The Greek has one tree.
ἀποσκηνόω has one translation, *to keep apart from*, so plain text; its second sense is only *= ἀποσκηνέω*, with no translation of its own.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads Μαμβρην; Coislinianus, M, has Μαμβρη.

reading: and having kept apart from [[name:Αβραμ]] [[having come|having come, having gone, having gone back and returned, having been going to and intended, having come within a little of and been near]] [[dwelt in|dwelt in, settled in, colonised, inhabited, settled and dwelt, lay and was situate]] [[to the side of|to the side of, motion alongside of, to, beside and near and by, passing by, beyond, contrary to and against, beside and except, on account of and because of and by means of, along the whole course of and during]] [[the tree|the tree, the oak, the wood, the worn-out old man]] the [[name:Μαμβρη]], which was, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, in [[name:Χεβρων]], and [[built a house|built a house, built, built for himself]] [[there|there, in that place]] an altar [[to lord|to lord, to master, to the one having power and authority over]].

names.gloss: (Μαμβρη, from Hebrew Mamrēʾ, of uncertain meaning)
(Χεβρων, from Hebrew Ḥebrôn, usually connected with ḥeber, "association")
